journey.name: DD-06 The relative wording stops seven days into the past as well
journey.description:
DD-04 walks the boundary forwards, at seven and eight days out. relativeDateOf has the same boundary behind it - the range check is written twice, once as 2..MAX_RELATIVE_DAYS and once as -MAX_RELATIVE_DAYS..-2 - and an off-by-one in the negative half would leave "Due 8 days ago" where a calendar date belongs, or a bare date where the count still reads better.
The past branch also carries the whole overdue story: the fourth seed row is the only overdue task the suite ever renders, and it is always exactly one day late. Anything further back has never been on screen.
A picker that refused a past date would fail at the third action, which is itself worth knowing: a due date in the past is a normal thing to record for a task that slipped.
"Due date" is the section label and starts with "Due " as well - exclude it when matching, the way DD-04 does.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0

actions.action: Select the date exactly seven days before today and tap "OK"
Verify that the due date reads "Due 7 days ago"
Select the date exactly eight days before today and tap "OK"
Verify that the due date no longer counts days and instead shows a calendar date, beginning with "Due " and excluding the "Due date" section label
Verify that the app returns to the "Tasks" screen
Verify that the "Book dentist" row shows that same calendar date
